recognize_zh: 箭頭指向一顆大型漿細胞，核偏位且小、有核周淡染區，細胞質非常豐富呈藍紫色；典型火焰細胞（flame cell）應有邊緣紅紫色的細胞質，此圖紅色邊緣不明顯，僅部分符合。
features: Large plasma cell (arrow) with voluminous blue-violet cytoplasm, several times the nuclear area
Small eccentric round nucleus with coarse chromatin and adjacent perinuclear hof
Cytoplasm with slightly mottled texture; a distinct magenta/red peripheral fringe is not evident
Background of maturing granulocytes, erythroid precursors, lymphocytes, and red cells
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a large plasma cell (arrow) with a small eccentric nucleus, perinuclear hof, and voluminous blue-violet cytoplasm. The cytoplasm appears slightly mottled but lacks a clearly defined red-purple peripheral fringe typical of classic flame cells. Background maturing myeloid and erythroid cells and small lymphocytes are present. Findings represent a plasma cell with abundant cytoplasm raising the possibility of a flame cell, which is associated with IgA-secreting plasma cell neoplasms but is not specific.

ddx.vs: Osteoblasts are larger, occur in clusters, and have an eccentric nucleus with a hof located away from, not adjacent to, the nucleus and lack immunoglobulin.
Mott cells contain discrete Russell body globules, whereas flame cells have diffuse cytoplasm with a magenta periphery due to glycoprotein-rich immunoglobulin.
Macrophages have a central or kidney-shaped nucleus without a hof and vacuolated cytoplasm with phagocytosed debris.
